assumptions: Thin-rim I = m R^2; spin-up at constant average torque over a labeled time.
c/I=0.05 /s and Kp/I=8 /s recycled from the isolator model (labeled).
Vane lever 0.30 m and vehicle radius of gyration 0.15 m are labeled drone-scale values.
Upper-stage Isp and mass fraction are the same optimistic labels as the parent search.
R=50 m and 250 m compact spinners are comparison assumptions, not vendor specs. HARP / SpinLaunch / StarTram named as well-known concepts only.

hold_speed_tube_to_mouth.note: Pulses until v_target, then an idealized hold that cancels g_along so speed is kept to the tube mouth.
Hold after target. A 300/450 s stage overshoots; ballistic residual is the best of this set.
Hold after target. Closest no-stage residual of the three hold cases.

powered_tube_note: Keeping the peak pusher on all the way to the mouth after v_target is reached overshoots badly at 100-1000 g (exit speeds of tens to hundreds of thousands of mph). Those runs are not useful configs; they show that the pusher must throttle. The hold-speed cases are the fair comparison to the unpowered tube coast.
